context:
Goal: on the iPhone you can type an Orphaned note, switch tabs and come back to the same draft.
Problem (goal): a drag that ends on the keys could mean hide only, or hide and save; the plan does not say, and only you can say whether a hidden keyboard may save your words.
Based on (read): the designer found no rule for it: the Card in Hand drag hides the keys and saves nothing there.
Departs from: main has no way to hide the keys in this form — either option adds the drag, one with a save and one without.
Waiting on: your answer on the keyboard question for the Orphaned form. This matters only if you pick the drag there.

options.gain: Same as Card in Hand; no surprise saves.
options.how: The drag hides the keys; the draft stays in the form as typed.
options.label: Hide the keys only
options.lose: A draft lost if the app closes before you save.

options.gain: The draft survives a closed app.
options.how: The drag also saves what you typed.
options.label: Hide the keys and save the draft
options.lose: A half-written note saved without you pressing Save.

title: When a drag hides the keys in the Orphaned form, should it also save the draft, or only hide the keys?
why: It matches how Card in Hand already behaves, and a save should be a press.
